01Arduino · Wireless

Bluetooth Control using HC-05

To control an Arduino circuit wirelessly from a mobile phone using Bluetooth.

See full details
Materials: Arduino UNO, HC-05 Bluetooth module, breadboard, jumper wires, LEDs, mobile phone with Bluetooth app, laptop.
Procedure: Fixed the HC-05 on the breadboard and wired it to the Arduino. Uploaded the code from the Arduino IDE. Paired the phone with HC-05. Pressed the power button in the app.
Observation: The Arduino circuit reacted to the commands sent from the phone app.
Result: Bluetooth can control a device from a distance without any wires.
02Arduino · Analog Input

Potentiometer Reading using Arduino

To read the changing value of a potentiometer using an analog pin of Arduino.

See full details
Materials: Arduino UNO, potentiometer, green jumper wires, USB cable, computer with Arduino IDE.
Procedure: Connected the three pins of the potentiometer to 5V, GND and an analog pin. Uploaded the code. Opened the Serial Monitor and turned the knob.
Observation: The numbers on the Serial Monitor changed as the knob was turned.
Result: A potentiometer gives a smooth, changing analog input to the Arduino.
03Arduino · Serial Monitor

Serial Monitor: Live Analog Values

To watch live sensor values on the Serial Monitor and understand the analog range.

See full details
Materials: Arduino UNO, potentiometer, jumper wires, USB cable, computer with Arduino IDE.
Procedure: Connected the potentiometer to the Arduino. Uploaded the code that prints the analog value. Opened the Serial Monitor and watched the numbers while changing the knob.
Observation: A fast list of numbers kept scrolling on the Serial Monitor and changed with the knob.
Result: Arduino converts the input voltage into numbers from 0 to 1023.
04Arduino · Wiring

Potentiometer Wiring and Testing

To learn how to wire the three pins of a potentiometer to Arduino and test it.

See full details
Materials: Arduino UNO, potentiometer, jumper wires, USB cable, computer with Arduino IDE.
Procedure: Joined the jumper wires to the potentiometer pins. Plugged them into the Arduino. Opened the Serial Monitor to check the readings.
Observation: After correct wiring, the Serial Monitor showed readings that changed when the knob was rotated.
Result: Correct wiring is important to get the right readings from a sensor.
05Arduino · Digital Output

LED Sequence with 4 LEDs

To light four LEDs one after another using the digital pins of Arduino.

See full details
Materials: Arduino UNO, 3 yellow LEDs, 1 red LED, resistor, breadboard, jumper wires, USB cable.
Procedure: Placed the LEDs on the breadboard. Connected each LED to a digital pin and joined the common ground. Uploaded the code and ran the program.
Observation: The LEDs glowed in a pattern, one after another.
Result: Arduino can control many outputs in a fixed order, just like a traffic light.
06Arduino · Basics

Single LED with Resistor

To light an LED safely using a resistor and an Arduino pin.

See full details
Materials: Arduino UNO, red LED, resistor, breadboard, jumper wires, USB cable.
Procedure: Connected the resistor in series with the LED. Joined one end to a digital pin and the other end to GND. Powered the Arduino through USB.
Observation: The red LED glowed when the circuit was powered.
Result: A resistor limits the current and protects the LED from damage.
07Arduino · Setup

Arduino UNO Setup and Wiring

To understand the Arduino UNO board and connect it with a computer.

See full details
Materials: Arduino UNO, USB cable, jumper wires, computer with Arduino IDE.
Procedure: Connected the board using the USB cable. Identified the power, digital and analog pins. Plugged the jumper wires into the correct pins.
Observation: The power LED on the board glowed and the board was ready to take code.
Result: Knowing the pins makes it easy to build circuits and upload programs.
08Arduino · Input and Output

Potentiometer with LED Circuit

To connect a potentiometer and an LED circuit with Arduino.

See full details
Materials: Arduino UNO, potentiometer, red LED, resistor, breadboard, jumper wires.
Procedure: Built the LED and resistor circuit on the breadboard. Connected the potentiometer wires to the Arduino pins.
Observation: The LED circuit and the potentiometer were wired together with the Arduino and powered through USB.
Result: A potentiometer can be used as an input to control an output like an LED.
